subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should `openclaw status` report external memory health from the live gateway runtime, or is the shipped `not checked` behavior sufficient outside `status --all` and `openclaw memory status --deep`?
rationale: Current main changed the wording but not the live-runtime health contract requested here, and there is both a broader open canonical issue and a conflicting open fork PR using closing syntax.

options.title: Make the broader live-gateway contract canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the owner-approved fix path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON output against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as sufficient
options.body: Declare the shipped behavior enough for this issue, close the conflicting fork PR, and document that detailed memory health belongs to `status --all` or `openclaw memory status --deep`.

recommendation.title: Make the broader live-gateway contract canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the owner-approved fix path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame and feature history put the status scan, memory-runtime, and gateway doctor boundary closest to steipete.
